gloss: more or less, tentatively, just in case

definitions.gloss: more or less, tentatively, for now
definitions.explanation: To a minimal acceptable degree, though not perfectly or completely.

definitions.gloss: just in case, just to be sure
definitions.explanation: As a precaution or for confirmation purposes.

examples.japanese: {一応|いちおう}⟦{終|お}わりました→終わる：00567_owaru⟧。
{一応|いちおう}⟦{分|わ}かりました→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
{一応|いちおう}⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦できています→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
{一応|いちおう}⟦{確認|かくにん}しておきます→確認：00158_kakunin⟧。
examples.english: I'll confirm just to be sure.

examples.japanese: {一応|いちおう}⟦{傘|かさ}→傘：00639_kasa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦いこう→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Let's take an umbrella just in case.

examples.japanese: {一応|いちおう}⟦{聞|き}いてみます→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: I'll ask just to be sure.

notes:
{一応|いちおう} is one of the most frequently used hedging words in Japanese. It softens assertions and adds nuance in two main ways.

SENSE 1 — "more or less":
Implies something meets a minimum standard but is not perfect or complete. Adds a tone of modesty or qualification.
- {一応|いちおう}⟦{終|お}わった→終わる：00567_owaru⟧: finished (but maybe not perfectly)
- {一応|いちおう}⟦{分|わ}かる→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧: I understand (to some extent)
- {一応|いちおう}⟦プロ→プロ：03871_puro⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧: I'm technically a professional (said modestly)

SENSE 2 — "just in case":
Indicates a precautionary action done for confirmation or safety.
- {一応|いちおう}⟦{確認|かくにん}→確認：00158_kakunin⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: check just to make sure
- {一応|いちおう}⟦{聞|き}いてみる→聞く：00483_kiku⟧: ask just in case
- {一応|いちおう}⟦{傘|かさ}→傘：00639_kasa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦いく→行く：00119_iku⟧: take an umbrella just in case

REGISTER:
Very common in casual and semi-formal speech. Frequently used in workplace communication to sound less assertive or to hedge politely.

WATCH OUT:
Learners sometimes confuse {一応|いちおう} with ⟦{一番|いちばん}→一番：01140_ichiban⟧ (most, number one) due to the shared ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧. They are unrelated in meaning.
